title: Induct the parcels onto the sorter lane single file, with a gap between them
instruction: Feed the four parcels from the blue tote onto the grey induction lane in single file: each lying flat between the rails with its long side along the lane, at least 10 cm of clear lane from the next parcel, and never side by side with or on top of another.
context: At a manual induction station a worker lays parcels from a jumbled tote onto a stopped or indexed sorter belt one behind another, long side along the belt and a hand's width apart, because the scanner and diverter treat parcels that touch or lie side by side as one item (a double feed: a no-read, a missort or a jam). Here the gap is made by the worker, not by the belt. Done by: postal mail sorters and processing machine operators, parcel hub package handlers.
setup: World frame for this text: 'in front' is away from the arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the robot's view. Induction lane (fixed): a grey painted MDF slab, 16 cm deep, 90 cm long and 10 mm thick, lying side to side across the front of both arms, its centre line 30 cm in front of the arm bases, from 52 cm right of the midline to 38 cm left of it. Two black steel rails, 10 mm wide and 15 mm tall, are fixed along its near and far edges, leaving 14 cm clear between them. Source tote (fixed): an open blue polypropylene tote, inside 24 cm front to back and 23.5 cm side to side, walls 10 mm thick and 6 cm tall, a 4 mm floor; its inside runs from 14 to 38 cm in front of the bases and from 40 to 63.5 cm left of the midline (in front of and beyond the left arm, past the lane's left end). Staging pad (fixed): a yellow plastic plate, 8 cm front to back, 12 cm side to side, 5 mm thick, centred on the midline 15 cm in front of the bases. Four loose corrugated-cardboard cartons start in the tote, all lying flat: a brown one (12 x 6 x 4 cm, 250 g), long side front to back, centred 20.5 cm in front of the bases and 47.5 cm left of the midline; an orange one (10 x 5 x 4.5 cm, 200 g) lying on top of the brown one, long side front to back, its centre 5 mm further from the arm bases than the brown one's (21 cm in front, 47.5 cm left); a red one (11 x 7 x 4 cm, 300 g), long side side to side, centred 30 cm in front and 46.5 cm left, its near face touching the brown carton's far end; a purple one (9 x 5.5 x 4.5 cm, 150 g), turned 45 degrees (its far end pointing toward the midline), centred 21 cm in front and 56.5 cm left, in the tote's near left corner. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A parcel is on the lane when any part of it is over the lane slab and its bottom is between 5 mm below and 2 cm above the lane's top, or at most 2 cm above the top of a parcel on the lane whose footprint it overlaps (a stack); a carton still carried higher is skipped. It is inducted when, at rest (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s), its footprint is between the rails (within 3 mm past a rail's inner face) and within the lane's ends, its bottom is within 5 mm of the lane's top, it is tilted at most 10 degrees from lying flat on one of its two largest faces (either way up: the cartons are unmarked), and its long side is within 15 degrees of the lane's length. Take the parcels on the lane in order along it; each neighbouring pair with both parcels inducted earns 0.25 if the clear lane between them (measured along the lane, between their nearest points) is at least 10 cm, or 0.1 if it is 5 to 10 cm, otherwise 0. A parcel on the lane that is not inducted breaks the pairs it is in; parcels not on the lane (in the tote, on the pad, on the table or floor) are skipped. 0.25 more when all four are inducted and all three gaps are at least 10 cm: 1.0 in all. There is no upper limit on a gap other than the lane's ends. The score is 0 if any two parcels on the lane are less than 1 cm apart along it, or overlap along it (side by side, stacked, or touching end to end): a double feed. The trial ends at 1.0 once all four are inducted with full gaps and at rest and this has held for 2.5 s; otherwise it scores the credit above at the last step.
reset_notes: Put the four cartons back in the tote as listed in the setup: the brown one flat, its long side front to back; the orange one on top of it; the red one across the tote touching the brown one's far end; the purple one turned 45 degrees in the near left corner. Tape outlines on the tote floor make this quick. The lane, rails, tote and pad stay fixed (clamp or tape them down).
fidelity: Approximate: the lane is a stopped belt modelled as a fixed slab, so nothing moves the parcels after they are laid down. Cartons are rigid boxes of uniform density with no labels, flaps or give. Every object, the lane and the tote included, has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than cardboard on a belt. The tote, pad and lane are fixed in place.
